comments.author: @ethniclove1
comments.text:
Lot's of corrections in your historical account.  The name Ayiti is one the original native and real names. Ayiti, Quisqueya, or Bohio based on the region of the Island, not St Domingue, name given only after by the colonist. The French, under the sun king Louis the XIV, claimed the western part of the island and called it St Domingue, mimicking the Spanish town of Santo Domingo in 1665, then when Spain formerly ceded the western part in 1697, St. Domingue became the richest asset to France, and no French territory had done so much for the French economy, because of the exploitation of African slaves as free labor. In 1804 : Following the Haitian Revolution, the independent nation reclaims the native name Haiti (Ayiti) during the reign of Napoleon Bonaparte, and slavery was abolished. The second free nation in the Americas, so small feat for a desperate but passionate group of enslaved people. Haiti is in this predicament today, simply because more than ninety percent of its population is black, and routed in their slavery past. The US, France, and the western world had adverse sentiments for its people. With stagnation and total abandonment from the rest of the world, it's difficult if not impossible to progress in a modern world, and that is their curse up to date, simply because once upon a time they dared to be free.

If one was to compare the birth of the United states as the first free nation in the America's from Great Britain, that story is pale in juste and noble cause to the birth of Haiti from France. One fought for the freedom to prosper independently and have slaves, the other fought to remain free and equal in the eyes of God. The only beacon of true freedom in all the America's if not the world, and that remains so even today, is Haiti,  A place that never received justice from the rest of the world.  My only and personal conclusion in all of this, are the comforting biblical words, "The first will be last, and the last will be first", maybe not in this world.
